title: Press Button
summary: A wall stands in front of the hovering aerial manipulator, and a push button is mounted flat on the wall's front face, facing the robot: a red circular plunger in a dark-grey circular housing. Press the button, i.e. push its spring-loaded plunger into the housing, along the wall's normal, until it is depressed by at least 4 mm (40 % of its 10 mm travel).
scene: The ground is the world's z = 0 plane. In front of the robot stands an immovable (kinematic) wall: a slab 0.1 m thick, 2.0 m wide and 2.0 m tall with a concrete-block surface, its front face turned toward the robot. Its distance, its sideways offset and a small tilt (the top leaning toward or away from the robot) vary between instances. On the wall's front face sits a push button: a dark-grey circular housing, 12 mm thick, fixed flush to the wall, and in front of it a red circular plunger, 10 mm thick, whose face stands about 2 cm proud of the wall surface. The plunger is the only moving part: it slides along the wall's normal into the housing (10 mm of travel) and is spring-loaded, returning to its rest position when not pushed. Where the button sits on the central part of the wall varies between instances, and so does its face size (plunger diameter between 6 and 12 cm, housing proportionally 1.2 times wider). Nothing moves by itself. The robot starts hovering level and motionless, facing the wall, with its arm at its zero joint configuration (end effector a little ahead of and above the airframe) and the gripper closed.
scene_privileged: One environment; its origin is the world origin. Robot at every reset: base_link at (0, 0, 1.0) m with orientation (1, 0, 0, 0) wxyz (body +x is the world +x direction), zero velocity; arm_link1_pitch_joint = arm_link2_pitch_joint = arm_link3_pitch_joint = arm_link4_roll_joint = 0 rad; arm_lfinger_joint = arm_rfinger_joint = 0.001 m (their lower limit: gripper closed, gripper_width 0.002 m). By the robot's URDF kinematics this puts ee_link at about (0.227, 0, 1.124) m with identity orientation and the tool-tip point (ee_link origin + 0.18 m along the ee_link x axis) at about (0.407, 0, 1.124) m; the end-effector command is initialised to the current ee_link pose. Wall: kinematic cuboid 0.1 (x) x 2.0 (y) x 2.0 (z) m, nominal centre (2.0, 0.0, 1.0) m and orientation identity (front face the plane x = centre_x - 0.05, normal -x, toward the robot); friction 1.0 static / 1.0 dynamic, restitution 0; visual material NVIDIA Concrete_Block.mdl. At each reset (Isaac Lab mdp.reset_root_state_uniform) the centre becomes (2.0 + dx, 0.0 + dy, 1.0) with dx, dy ~ U(-0.2, 0.2) m independently, and the orientation becomes quat_from_euler_xyz(0, pitch, 0) with pitch ~ U(-0.2, 0.2) rad (a rotation about the world y axis through the wall centre; positive pitch tilts the top of the wall away from the robot, the front normal turning upward). Button: articulation push_button.usd with a fixed root (housing) and self-collisions disabled. At each reset, after the wall, its root is placed at wall_centre + R_wall (-0.05, by, bz) with by, bz ~ U(-0.3, 0.3) m independently (a point on the wall's front face, offset in the wall's own y-z plane) and given the wall's orientation, so the button's local +x is the wall normal pointing into the wall. Housing: cylinder along local x, radius 0.072 s, thickness 0.012 m (local x from -0.012 to 0), mass 0.5 kg, colour (0.1, 0.1, 0.1). Plunger (body 'plunger'; AM-Bench's goal_pos observation is its position): cylinder radius 0.06 s, thickness 0.01 m, authored at local x = -0.015 (its face about 2 cm in front of the wall surface), mass 0.02 kg, colour (0.9, 0.1, 0.1). Button physics material: static friction 0.6, dynamic 0.5, restitution 0.1. Prismatic joint PlungerSlideJoint along the button's local +x (positive = plunger pushed toward the wall), limits [0, 0.01] m, reset to 0 m with zero velocity every episode; Isaac Lab implicit actuator with stiffness 1000 N/m and damping 80 N s/m toward the target 0 m, effort limit 20 N, velocity limit 5 m/s. Scale s (applied to the button's local y and z only: face radius changes, thickness does not) ~ U(0.5, 1.0), drawn once when the environment is created (a prestartup event), not at each reset. Scene default physics material: friction 1.0 / 1.0, restitution 0.
success: Success when the button's prismatic joint PlungerSlideJoint has position >= 0.004 m (button_pressed_threshold; the joint ranges from 0 m, unpressed, to 0.01 m, fully pressed; positive = plunger pushed into the housing toward the wall). Evaluated after every control step (decimation 1, so after every 1/120 s physics step) on the simulated state; no hold time is required. The episode terminates at the first step where it holds. Otherwise it is truncated by the time limit: episode_length_s = 20 s, i.e. max_episode_length = 2400 control steps; AM-Bench raises the time-out when episode_length_buf >= max_episode_length - 1, i.e. at the 2399th step.
difficulty_note: The target is small (as little as 6 cm across), its place on the wall and the wall's tilt change per instance, and the plunger springs back: the 4 mm depression has to be produced by pushing along the (possibly tilted) wall normal from a free-flying, hovering base.
standard_notes: The button's pose and its pressed state are not given: the red disc on the concrete wall has to be found with the forward-looking onboard cameras and related to the robot through proprioception (base and end-effector poses). A press shows only as a few millimetres of plunger travel, and success is not reported during the episode.
